implementation_notes: The general realization is the hand-written Concept/Model wrapper (external polymorphism): a nested abstract Concept declares the operations plus a virtual destructor and clone; a template Model<T> marked final stores the value and forwards; the public wrapper is a non-templated value type holding unique_ptr<Concept> (or an inline buffer for small-buffer optimisation) whose template constructor performs the binding. Sean Parent's value-semantic refinement adds clone through the concept so the handle stays regular. For the two dominant contracts the standard library already ships the erasure - std::function (C++11) for callables, std::any (C++17) for opaque copyable values, std::move_only_function (C++23) when the callable owns move-only state - so hand-roll only when the behaviour set is neither callability nor a bare value. Boost.TypeErasure generalizes the hand-written form with named concepts.
pitfalls: Forgetting the virtual destructor (or a type-erased deleter): destroying through Concept is undefined behaviour.
Losing value semantics: without clone() the wrapper is move-only, so it cannot be stored in ordinary containers or returned by value as intended.
Template-constructor errors surface deep inside Model<T> instantiation; add a C++20 requires-clause or a static_assert in the constructor so a type missing an operation fails at the binding site.
ABI: a unique_ptr<Concept>-based wrapper built against a different standard library is not layout-compatible - do not hand one across a binary plugin boundary.

variants.name: Standard-library erased wrappers (std::function / std::any)
variants.implementation_notes: The standard library provides the erasure for the two most common contracts, so no wrapper is written: std::function<R(Args...)> holds any callable with that signature (function pointer, capturing lambda, member-function pointer, functor) and std::any holds any copy-constructible value with type-safe recovery via any_cast. Choose this form when the shared behaviour is 'callable with this signature' or 'an opaque value the consumer will cast back', and the general Concept/Model wrapper when the erased interface has named operations. C++23's std::move_only_function lifts the CopyConstructible requirement for callables owning move-only state.
variants.code_sketch:
std::function<int(int)> f = [](int x) { return x + 1; };  // any callable
std::any v = std::string{"hello"};                      // any copyable value
v = 42;                                                 // unrelated types, no common base
// custom behaviour sets still need the hand-written wrapper (default variant).
pitfalls: std::function requires a CopyConstructible callable, so it silently refuses lambdas capturing a unique_ptr - capture a shared_ptr or move to std::move_only_function.

std::any erases the value but no behaviour: every use is an any_cast back to the exact type, and a mismatch throws bad_any_cast, so std::any is not a substitute for a concept when operations are needed.
Both wrappers may allocate when the stored object does not fit their small-buffer optimisation, and neither preserves ordering or equality beyond what the stored type exposes.
